title: source-gates reads README.md and LICENSE, but the push trigger paths omit both, so a push touching only those gets no push-triggered run
description:
Reported by opum-agent under OPAG-432 AC3 (2026-09-25), from its fleet audit tooling/fleet-sweep/bin/paths-coverage-audit.mjs (opum-ai/opum-agent#1030). The audit asks whether a required job's push paths filter covers every file the job reads. Same class as QCLI-376, whose fix (opum-ai/quest-cli#283, 9871531) did not cover this. opum-agent ran the controls by ref: at 4bd161a (9871531's parent) the audit lists QCLI-376's five files plus README.md; at 9871531 it lists README.md only.

VERIFIED HERE at origin/dev 0b26cf7, by git show, not taken from the relay. source-gates runs scripts/qualification/prepublish.mjs, which always runs the package_contents_and_provenance gate (bun run check:packages, i.e. scripts/check-package-artifacts.mjs). That script:
(1) README.md, CONTENT gate. It extracts package/README.md from the packed root tarball (line 272) and fails on version-claim marker errors or a version token outside a claim region (lines 286-353).
(2) LICENSE, PRESENCE gate only, found here and NOT in the audit's output. The root pack contents must be exactly LICENSE, README.md, bin/quest.cjs and package.json (line 88), so deleting or renaming the root LICENSE fails the gate. package.json files lists README.md and LICENSE.
.github/workflows/prepublication-qualification.yml push paths list neither README.md nor LICENSE. The pull_request trigger is unfiltered, so a PR still gets one source-gates row. What is lost is the push-triggered run on dev, and with it the dev-SHA source-gates row a fast-forward promotion needs before a PR exists (see the CLAUDE.md profile section on source-gates and ABSENT).

NOT MEASURED: whether the audit reads presence-only dependencies such as LICENSE at all. If it does not, it has a second blind spot, worth reporting to opum-agent when this lands.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The push trigger paths in prepublication-qualification.yml include README.md and LICENSE, or the task records a written reason for leaving either out
A re-run of opum-agent paths-coverage-audit.mjs against the fixing ref reports no omission for quest-cli, cited with its ref and output
opum-agent is told whether its audit reads presence-only dependencies such as LICENSE, with the LICENSE case as the test

plan: 1. Verify the gap at the current dev head by reading the workflow paths and the gate script reads.
2. Add README.md and LICENSE to the push paths, annotated in the file existing style.
3. Fetch opum-agent paths-coverage-audit.mjs and read it to answer the presence-only question with the LICENSE case (AC 3).
4. Run that audit against the fixing ref and capture ref plus output for AC 2.
5. Gates: bun run check and lore check.
6. Deliver per opum-sdlc; close in the PR; report the AC 3 answer and AC 2 citation to opum-agent.
implementationNotes:
SESSION HANDOFF and standing state at the opum-workflow 0.10.12 restart wave (opum-agent OPAG-729, 2026-09-29). QCLI-377 is next up; this note is where it stands.

CLAIMED, not started: status In Progress, the plan is recorded above, and no source change has been made yet. The verified cause, re-read at dev head fd91cdd5 by reading the files rather than the record: .github/workflows/prepublication-qualification.yml lists neither README.md nor LICENSE in its push paths (a grep for either returns zero hits in the file), while scripts/check-package-artifacts.mjs genuinely reads both -- LICENSE as a presence gate in the packed-file lists at lines 74 and 88 (the root pack must be exactly LICENSE, README.md, bin/quest.cjs and package.json), and README.md as a content gate through the packed README version-claim assertions from line 272 on. The pull_request trigger is unfiltered, so what is lost is only the push-triggered run on dev, and with it the dev-SHA row a fast-forward promotion needs before a promotion PR exists.

THE FIX (AC 1): add README.md and LICENSE to that push paths list, annotated with this task id in the file existing comment style (compare the QCLI-376 and QCLI-328 blocks already there). No gate change is needed. Worth keeping in view: the feature branch will touch the workflow file, so source-gates will fire twice on its head -- once per trigger -- and the merge to dev will carry both rows.

THE ASK AT THIS TASK BOUNDARY (ACs 2 and 3, both need opum-agent): AC 2 wants opum-agent paths-coverage-audit.mjs re-run against the fixing ref, cited with its ref and output. That tool lives in the opum-agent repository at tooling/fleet-sweep/bin/paths-coverage-audit.mjs and imports ../lib/paths-coverage.mjs and ../lib/fleet.mjs, so fetch the whole tooling/fleet-sweep tree, not the bin file alone. It reads by gh api and mutates nothing. Usage: node bin/paths-coverage-audit.mjs --repo quest-cli --ref <sha>, with --record <file> to capture the bytes read. Two practical traps measured this session: quote any gh api URL containing a question mark (an unquoted ?recursive=1 is glob-expanded by zsh and fails, the same trap this repository profile already records), and read lib/paths-coverage.mjs before trusting a clean result, because AC 3 asks whether the audit even sees presence-only dependencies such as LICENSE -- the LICENSE case is the test. If it cannot, that blind spot is the finding to report back to opum-agent.

WHAT ELSE MOVED AT THIS BOUNDARY, for orientation: QCLI-311 is Done and promoted -- main is fd91cdd5, a fast-forward of dev, the ordinary promotion path. QCLI-412 (extend the completion staging hint to close, archive and demote; ruled execution) and QCLI-413 (the same hint under --json; a contract change that needs an operator A/B through opum-agent before any pickup, and NOT started) were filed from opum-agent instruction. Neither is this task; do not absorb them.

ACs 1-3 evidence. Audit tool read at opum-agent dev 038182d30eaddd90c65c21c6f1427c6d2c31c261 (tooling/fleet-sweep), fetched by gh api -- never from a sibling working tree.

AC1 DONE. The push paths in .github/workflows/prepublication-qualification.yml now list README.md and LICENSE, commented with this task id in the file's existing style. No gate changed.

AC2 DONE, run as a TWO-SIDED CONTROL in one invocation with the same tool. The control is load-bearing: a pass on the fixing ref alone cannot tell "covered" from "the audit read nothing here".
- CONTROL, pre-fix ref 2ecc6d3cf5aef1128a4aa2414f1a0ee2905ad0b4 (origin/dev): exit 6, "2 omission(s)". Both reported OMITTED on push for source-gates, each with its via chain -- step 5 / bun scripts/qualification/prepublish.mjs / ... / run check:packages / script check:packages / bun run scripts/check-package-artifacts.mjs / scripts/check-package-artifacts.mjs.
- FIXING ref 387909897f2e365f89abee50e1df7eb9bf7cf486: exit 0, "Nothing omitted that the heuristic can see." source-gates reads 73 files, push:paths, covered.
- Both runs report what they read -- 1/1 repositories, 7 workflow file(s), 3 required job(s), 109 followed script file(s) -- so the clean result is not an empty read, per the tool's own absence discipline (OPAG-268).

AC3 ANSWERED: YES, the audit reads presence-only dependencies such as LICENSE, and LICENSE is the test -- it appears BY NAME in the pre-fix output above, not inferred from another path. It is seen because it is a real file at the audited ref: lib/paths-coverage.mjs keeps a token with neither a slash nor an extension only when it is exactly a file in the tree (the bare() rule, OPAG-435), and the executed entry's quoted-literal scan then adds it.

WHY THIS TASK'S OWN NOTE SAID OTHERWISE: the description records LICENSE as "NOT in the audit's output", which was accurate when written at 0b26cf7. The audit dropped extensionless files then. opum-agent filed and fixed exactly that as OPAG-435 (Done 2026-09-25; "paths-coverage-audit drops extensionless files such as LICENSE, so a gate reading one is reported as covered"; tooling/fleet-sweep/lib/paths-coverage.mjs, commits a96a045/3a29c94), read from its tracker at origin/dev. The run above is the fixed audit. So the open question this task carried is answered as "it had that blind spot, it was found and fixed four days ago, and this is the confirming measurement" -- not "it still has one".

RESIDUAL BLIND SPOT, unmeasured against a live case and stated by the tool's own BLIND_SPOTS on every run: an extensionless file the job reads but the audited ref LACKS, or one a step CREATES, is still unseen. A gate reading a generated LICENSE would not be caught.

Delivered in opum-ai/quest-cli#422, whose head 3879098 carries the source change; the run cited in the final summary covers that commit.
finalSummary:
The push trigger's paths in .github/workflows/prepublication-qualification.yml now list README.md and LICENSE, annotated QCLI-377 in the file's existing comment style. source-gates runs scripts/check-package-artifacts.mjs, which reads both -- README.md as the packed npm page's version-claim content gate, LICENSE as a presence gate on the root pack's exact file list -- so a push touching only one of them fired no push-triggered run, and left no source-gates row on that dev SHA for a fast-forward promotion to consume before a PR exists. No gate changed; pull_request stays unfiltered, so a PR still gets its row.

VERIFIED:
- AC1: both entries are in the push paths, and the workflow parses -- GitHub accepted and ran it on this branch. No gate logic touched.
- AC2: opum-agent's tooling/fleet-sweep/bin/paths-coverage-audit.mjs, fetched at opum-agent dev 038182d, run as a TWO-SIDED CONTROL in one invocation (a pass on the fixing ref alone cannot tell "covered" from "read nothing here"). CONTROL, pre-fix 2ecc6d3cf5aef1128a4aa2414f1a0ee2905ad0b4 (origin/dev): exit 6, "2 omission(s)" -- LICENSE and README.md, both OMITTED on push for source-gates, each with its via chain. FIXING ref 387909897f2e365f89abee50e1df7eb9bf7cf486: exit 0, "Nothing omitted that the heuristic can see"; source-gates reads 73 files on push:paths, covered. Both runs report reading 1/1 repositories, 7 workflow file(s), 3 required job(s), 109 followed script file(s), so the clean result is not an empty read.
- AC3: answered by measurement, not inference -- LICENSE appears BY NAME in the pre-fix output above, so the audit does read presence-only dependencies. This task's own note that LICENSE was absent from the audit's output was accurate when written and is now stale: it was opum-agent OPAG-435 (Done 2026-09-25), which fixed the audit dropping extensionless files. The residual blind spot the tool still prints on every run: an extensionless file the audited ref LACKS, or one a step CREATES, is unseen.

GATES: bun run check -- 993 pass, 0 fail, exit 0 (a &&-chain whose last step is the test suite, so completion proves every earlier step). lore check -- exit 0, 63 files, 0 errors.

DELIVERY: opum-ai/quest-cli#422. The source change at 3879098 is covered by Prepublication qualification run 36536355234 (push) and run 36536946969 (pull_request), both completed/success on that SHA, alongside Tracker integrity run 36536947016 and lore check run 36536946967.
